.... FOURTH INNINGS ...

Australia have declared their innings and have set India a target of 444 runs! Having led by 296 runs at the start of the day, Australia lost an early wicket and got their day off to a cautious start. With 30 minutes to go for Lunch, they lost Cameron Green but they continued to score at a brisk rate. After Lunch, Alex Carey and Mitchell Starc decided to throw their hands at everything and India's decision of taking the second new ball helped their cause big time. They added 69 runs to their score at Lunch and have set a mighty total for India to overhaul. On the other hand, India had their moments early in the day but could not keep things quiet, leaking a lot of runs. India's openers now face the tough task of dealing with the Aussie new ball attack. Can Rohit Sharma and Co. rise to the challenge? Let's find out as India's reply is coming up shortly...

They stride out to the centre and take their respective field positions. It will be Ravindra Jadeja to start the proceedings with the ball for India. Lets's play...
... DAY 4, SESSION 2 ...

At the start of the day, India needed early wickets to have a shot at winning this Test. The move to start with Umesh Yadav from one end rewarded India with a breakthrough in his second over of the day. Moreover, Ravindra Jadeja's ploy to bowl in the rough worked as well. Having reduced Australia to 167-6, India would have fancied themselves to pick a couple of wickets more before Lunch but they were unable to do so. The Indian bowlers have fought hard in the second innings and when they come back after Lunch, they would want to put a squeeze on things and at the same time, bowl Australia out as quickly as possible. Can India manage to keep Australia's lead under 400? We shall find out soon as the players return for the second session at 5.40 pm IST (12.10 pm GMT).

SESSION SUMMARY - 78 runs, 26 overs, 2 wickets. Another absorbing session of Test cricket comes to an end and it is Australia who continue to be in a dominant position. Having begun the day 296 runs ahead, Australia were rocked early, losing their overnight batter Marnus Labuschagne. Alex Carey then came out with a positive approach and steadied the ship with Cameron Green. Despite losing Green, Carey continued punishing loose deliveries and thanks to him, Australia's lead has now swelled to 374 runs. On a wicket having variable bounce, chasing anything over 350 is never going to be easy but Australia would want to bat India out of the game in the second session.

PITCH REPORT - Nasser Hussain starts by saying that it is a stunning day in South London and informs that Day 4 will be the warmest day of the Test. Adds that there is a 7% chance of rain but feels that it will stay away. Mentions that it is a new ball pitch and there is a vast difference in bounce between the new and old ball. Ravi Shastri joins him and says that the cracks have opened up and they are on the natural lengths for Mohammed Siraj and Pat Cummins. Reckons that reaction time is marginal when new ball pitches on these cracks. Looking at the rough, he says that it is not going to be easy for left-handed batters. Adds that it looks good from India's point of view since they have only a left-hander in Ravindra Jadeja. Ends by saying that chasing anything over 375 will be tough for India but expects them to go for the win.

Having started Day 3 on the back foot, India lost KS Bharat on the second ball of the day and were staring at conceding a huge first innings lead. Ajinkya Rahane and Shardul Thakur then got together and stitched a fighting stand. Once Rahane was dismissed, the tail was unable to wag and India were bowled out for 296 runs. India showed a much improved bowling display in the second innings and did not allow Australia to run away with the game. If India are to have any chance of winning this Test, early wickets on Day 4 will be key. Can Mohammed Siraj and Co. swing the match in India’s favour? Stick around to see how things pan out on Day 4.

Australia were off to the best possible start on Day 3 as Scott Boland struck in his very first over. However, they were unable to capitalise on this early scalp in what was a frustrating first session for them. The Aussie bowlers roared back in the second session and bundled India out to take a first-innings lead of 173 runs. In reply, they were off to a cautious start and ended the day with a lead of 296 runs and 6 wickets in hand. Australia would want to bat the whole first session and take a call on a declaration after Lunch.

Hello and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen, to our coverage of Day 4 of the 2021–23 World Test Championship final between Australia and India at the Kennington Oval in London. We have had three days of entertaining action with the game ebbing and flowing and it is Australia who find themselves in a strong position to call the shots.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1 …

Australia have been well ahead right from Day 1 and they have consolidated their position even further on this moving day of the Test match. India are grasping at strings at the moment and they already need a massive batting effort in their second inning to pull off a miraculous run chase. How long will the Aussies bat on Day 4? Or will India be able to bowl out their opponents early and take the momentum into their batting? The action continues on Saturday 10th June for Day 4 of this ultimate Test match and the first ball will be bowled at 3 pm IST (9.30 am GMT) but do join us early for the build-up. Cheers!

India's star with the bat, Ajinkya Rahane is in for a chat. He informs that he is feeling alright despite the blow on the right index finger. Adds that it is painful but manageable and says that it will not affect his batting in the second innings. Mentions that he is really happy with the way he batted and feels that the partnership with Ravindra Jadeja and Shardul Thakur was crucial. Reckons that bowlers bowled well in the second innings and it is a good effort to reduce Australia to 123-4. On the catch by Cameron Green, he says that he is a good fielder with a big reach. Feels that Australia are slightly ahead in the game but feels that the first hour on Day 4 will be crucial as a bowling unit.

India started the day with their backs against the wall and things got worse for them when KS Bharat was dismissed on the second delivery of the morning. However, after that came the fightback from India as Ajinkya Rahane and Shardul Thakur held the fort right up till Lunch putting on 109 runs together for the 7th wicket. Rahane reached his half-century and looked destined for his 13th hundred but was dismissed by Pat Cummins right after the break. The Australian skipper dismissed Umesh Yadav soon after but Shardul managed to reach his half-century as he played an outstanding rearguard knock. He was dismissed by Cameron Green and Mohammad Shami lost his wicket to Mitchell Starc in the quest for some quick runs. With a lead of 173, Australia started their second innings in a circumspect way and David Warner lost his wicket to Mohammed Siraj which had the Indians believing they were still in the game going into the Tea interval.

SESSION SUMMARY - 100 runs, 33 overs, 3 wickets. Day 3 has definitely been a moving day and Australia are well on top of this game. They have taken a massive lead of 296 runs and still have 6 wickets in hand having worn out the Indians in the field with some good batting. They went into Tea at 23 for the loss of one wicket and the Indian bowlers bowled some tight lines after the break. They were rewarded for their persistence when Umesh Yadav got Usman Khawaja driving away from his body and found his outside edge through to the keeper. A 62-run partnership between Steven Smith and Marnus Labuschagne shifted the momentum back in Australia’s favor as they scored briskly but Smith was dismissed playing a poor shot. Ravindra Jadeja was the one who got the breakthrough and he kept the pressure up with some tight bowling. He had a chance dropped by Umesh Yadav in the deep but it did not prove costly as two balls later he held onto one off his own bowling to send Travis Head back to the shed. Marnus battled on and is 9 runs short of his half-century and Cameron Green has managed to survive at the wicket.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the third and final session on Day 3. The two umpires make their way out to the middle followed by Usman Khawaja and ​​​​Marnus Labuschagne. The Indian players now stride out to the centre as well. It will be Mohammad Shami to start the proceedings with the ball for India. Off we go...
... DAY 3, SESSION 3 ...

Australia had to pick up their performance after a disappointing morning session and they did so quickly with their skipper Pat Cummins. He broke the 100-plus run partnership but the credit goes to Cameron Green who pulled off a remarkable catch. Cummins struck once again soon after before Cameron Green and Mitchell Starc picked up the last two wickets to wrap up the Indian inning inside an hour in the second session of Day 3. They had a lead of 173 going into the innings break and got off to a tentative start in their second outing. David Warner was the casualty of their failed opening partnership as he departed on one but since then Marnus Labuschagne and Usman Khawaja have steadied the ship. The last session of the moving day of the Test match should determine if India still have a chance to win this game but they need wickets in a hurry. Or will Australia bat them out of this tie? Do join us at 8 pm IST (2.30 pm GMT) to find out how the final session of Day 3 plays out.

SESSION SUMMARY - 59 runs, 20.4 overs, 5 wickets. What an exciting Test match we have witnessed so far! India fought back brilliantly in the first session and would have loved to continue the good work post Lunch but things did not go as planned for them. Ajinkya Rahane could not add any runs to his score and departed right after the break to provide the opponents with an opening. Umesh Yadav looked to hang around but that ploy did not work as he found his stumps shattered in an attempt to play defensively. This prompted Shardul Thakur and Mohammad Shami to go after the bowling and they played some good shots to push the total close to the 300-run mark. Shardul reached his half-century but both perished in the quest for quick runs. India were eventually bowled out for 296 but they came out strong with the ball. Mohammed Siraj drew first blood and the opening bowlers have kept it tight but they will know they have loads of work to do here to save this game as the Aussies lead by 196 with 9 wickets in hand.
On a shortish length, on off, Marnus Labuschagne goes back and pushes it to the right of mid on for a single. That will be Tea on Day 3!
